title: Generative Language Models for Disease Treatment Recommendations: A Systematic Literature Review

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Generative Language Models for Disease Treatment Recommendations: A Systematic Literature Review》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · Par7】This systematic literature review (SLR) aims to critically evaluate the current state of GenAI, focused on language models, in providing treatment recommendations across various medical conditions. The primary objectives are to understand their applicability in diverse medical domains and identify potential limitations and challenges in their real-world implementation. By analyzing peer-reviewed works and key findings, this review seeks to offer comprehensive insights into the capabilities of language models, their integration challenges, and the ethical considerations that must be navigated to harness their full potential in healthcare.

【Introduction · Par2】The evolution of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) technologies has brought a new era of possibilities across various sectors, including healthcare. The introduction of the transformer architecture by Vaswani et al. [1] made possible the rise of models like Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT) [2] and Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [3], which revolutionized tasks in natural language processing (NLP), extending their utility to medical decision-making. These models, characterized by their advanced deep learning architectures and extensive training datasets, are increasingly being employed to assist healthcare professionals by providing personalized treatment recommendations, thus potentially improving patient outcomes and optimizing clinical workflows.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Generative Language Models for Disease Treatment Recommendations: A Systematic Literature Review》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Methodology · Par21】The objective of this SLR is to critically evaluate the application of GenAI in providing treatment recommendations across various medical conditions. To report this, we adhere to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Our review is composed of an initial search, and a supplementary search, reported in the following sections. The SLR seeks to address the following nine Research Questions (RQs):(RQ1) In which diseases have GenAI been applied for treatment recommendations?(RQ2) What types of GenAI models have been utilized for generating disease treatment recommendations?(RQ3) What types of treatments have been considered in GenAI-based recommendations?(RQ4) How is prompt engineering used in GenAI-based treatment recommendations?(RQ5) How are datasets used for GenAI training?(RQ6) How are GenAI models evaluated for treatment recommendations?(RQ7) What ethical and regulatory considerations arise from the use of GenAI in medical treatment recommendations?(RQ8) What are the common challenges and limitations associated with the implementation of GenAI in clinical practice?(RQ9) What future research directions are suggested by current works on GenAI for treatment recommendation?

【Methodology · Par26】(RQ5) How are datasets used for GenAI training?

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Generative Language Models for Disease Treatment Recommendations: A Systematic Literature Review》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · Par76】The initial search resulted in 31 works, 27 from the database search and 4 from the snowballing technique. The supplementary search resulted in 12 works included. In total, this SLR analyzes 42 relevant works. The following sections will address and discuss each research question defined earlier in our methodology.

【Conclusions and Future Directions · Par169】This study has systematically explored the application of GenAI models in providing treatment recommendations for various diseases, highlighting both the advances and the existing research gaps. Although GenAI technologies demonstrate potential for optimizing clinical decision-making and personalizing patient care, significant barriers remain, such as limited real-world validation, risks of bias, and regulatory uncertainties. Furthermore, most research efforts have focused on general-purpose models lacking fine-tuning on specialized medical data.

【(RQ8) What are the common Challenges and Limitations Associated with the Implementation of GenAI in Clinical Practice? · Par147】The integration of GenAI into clinical practice presents several challenges and limitations that slow down its widespread adoption and effectiveness. Based on the reviewed literature, the most frequently cited issues relate to reliability, bias and ethics, transparency, scalability, computational costs, regulatory concerns, and performance in complex scenarios. To summarize these challenges, Table 7 presents a structured overview of the key challenges associated with the implementation of GenAI in clinical practice, along with the corresponding works that have explored these issues.

【(RQ8) What are the common Challenges and Limitations Associated with the Implementation of GenAI in Clinical Practice? · Par148】One of the predominant concerns is reliability, as GenAI models are susceptible to generating hallucinations, inconsistencies, and overly generic responses, this is mentioned in 28 studies (Table 7). These issues arise from the data-dependent nature of these models, which can lead to incorrect or misleading medical advice [47]. Given that clinical decision-making relies on accuracy and precision, this limitation raises significant concerns regarding patient safety.
